description: Canonical registry of every source the DriftGuard SOC 2 knowledge base may cite. All knowledge records reference sources by source_id only; bibliographic detail lives here and nowhere else.

authority_tiers.name: Authoritative requirement
authority_tiers.definition: Text that determines whether a SOC 2 examination or report conforms. Issued by a standard setter with authority over SOC 2 (AICPA ASEC / ASB). Only these sources may be described as required.
authority_tiers.citation_obligation: Mandatory. Any statement using 'must', 'is required', or 'the criteria state' MUST cite a tier-1 source.

authority_tiers.name: Official guidance
authority_tiers.definition: Non-binding interpretive material published by the standard setter (AICPA guides, description criteria, points of focus commentary). Explains how criteria are commonly applied; is not itself a requirement.
authority_tiers.citation_obligation: Required for interpretive claims. Must be labelled as guidance, never as requirement.

authority_tiers.name: Industry guidance
authority_tiers.definition: Recognised external frameworks and standards used to operationalise criteria (COSO, NIST, ISO, CIS). Useful for control design and cross-framework mapping. Carries no SOC 2 authority.
authority_tiers.citation_obligation: Required when used as the basis of a mapping or a control-design recommendation.

authority_tiers.name: Auditor interpretation
authority_tiers.definition: Practitioner judgement about how service auditors typically evaluate a criterion, including common testing approaches and evidence expectations. Varies by firm and engagement.
authority_tiers.citation_obligation: Must be explicitly labelled as interpretation and hedged ('auditors commonly', 'is typically expected'). Never phrased as a requirement.

authority_tiers.name: DriftGuard best practice
authority_tiers.definition: DriftGuard's own opinionated recommendation. Represents product judgement, not external authority.
authority_tiers.citation_obligation: Must be attributed to DriftGuard and clearly separated from criteria language.

sources.title: TSP Section 100, 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (With Revised Points of Focus - 2022)
sources.citation_hint: Cite individual criteria by identifier, e.g. TSC CC6.1.
sources.notes: The 2022 revision updated points of focus only; the criteria themselves are unchanged since 2017. Points of focus are not requirements and need not be individually addressed.

sources.title: Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements No. 21, Direct Examination Engagements
sources.edition: Issued September 2020; effective for reports dated on or after June 15, 2022
sources.citation_hint: Cite for the attestation standard governing SOC 2 examinations.
sources.notes: Created AT-C section 206 (no SOC impact), superseded AT-C section 205 (retitled 'Assertion-Based Examination Engagements') and amended AT-C section 105. Introduced no substantive change to SOC 2 report content.

sources.title: AT-C Section 105, Concepts Common to All Attestation Engagements
sources.citation_hint: Cite for practitioner independence, competence, and general attestation requirements.

sources.title: AT-C Section 205, Assertion-Based Examination Engagements
sources.citation_hint: Cite for examination-level evidence, opinion, and modification requirements.
sources.notes: Superseded the SSAE No. 18 version of AT-C 205 and was retitled by SSAE No. 21.

sources.title: DC Section 200, 2018 Description Criteria for a Description of a Service Organization's System in a SOC 2 Report
sources.citation_hint: Cite for what management's system description must contain.
sources.notes: Distinct from the trust services criteria: the description criteria govern the system description, the trust services criteria govern the controls. VERIFY the enumeration and count of individual DC items against the published text before asserting them.

sources.title: AICPA Guide, SOC 2: Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, or Privacy
sources.citation_hint: Cite for interpretive guidance on scoping, testing, and reporting.
sources.notes: Updated periodically. Confirm the edition in force before quoting specific paragraph numbers.

sources.title: Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013)
sources.publisher: Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO)
sources.citation_hint: Cite for the 17 internal control principles underpinning common criteria CC1-CC5.
sources.notes: Incorporated by reference into the trust services criteria; the common criteria are organised around the COSO principles.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.citation_hint: Cite for cross-framework control mappings and implementation detail.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection - Information security management systems - Requirements
sources.citation_hint: Cite Annex A control identifiers for cross-framework mapping.
sources.notes: Copyrighted text. Do not reproduce control wording in the knowledge base; reference identifiers only.

sources.title: CIS Critical Security Controls, Version 8
sources.citation_hint: Cite safeguard identifiers for implementation-level guidance.

sources.title: DriftGuard Auditor Practice Notes
sources.citation_hint: Cite for statements about how service auditors commonly test or what they typically expect.
sources.notes: Internal collection of practitioner judgement. Content cited to this source MUST be hedged and MUST NOT be presented as a SOC 2 requirement. Firm practice varies.

sources.title: DriftGuard Recommended Practice
sources.citation_hint: Cite for DriftGuard's own recommendations, defaults, thresholds, and freshness expectations.
sources.notes: Product opinion. Never presented to a customer as an audit requirement.
